4.text: Fall Ceremonial. — The time of the fall ceremonial varies, in different

5.text: villages and families, from the end of October to the first days of January.

6.text: The fittest time, however, is thought to be at the birth of the moon after

7.text: the shortest days of the winter, and it is considered the beginning of the

8.text: first month.¹ Moreover, in villages like Uñiˊsak or Uweˊlen, the ceremonial

9.text: lasts more than a month, and thus the celebrations of the last families come

10.text: into the second half of January. Where there is a “front-house family,” it

11.text: begins the course. In other villages — such, for instance, as Čeˊčin, Aˊčon,

12.text: or Uñiˊsak — without a “front-house family,” there is no particular order for

13.text: the ceremonials, and it changes from year to year by mere accident.

14.text: The Chukchee have two different methods of celebrating this ceremonial.

15.text: The simpler one is called “genuine thanksgiving ceremonial” (lɪˊê-mñêˊɪrg̣ɪn).

16.text: Even the name shows that this ceremonial is identified with the ordinary

17.text: thanksgiving ceremonial which was described previously. The other method

18.text: is, properly speaking, a repetition of the ceremony of Kereˊtkun, Karaˊtko-

19.text: vaˊɪrg̣ɪn. The choice of either method varies in different villages, and even

20.text: among individual families. Nevertheless, as far as can be observed, the

21.text: “genuine thanksgiving ceremonial” is more in use among those families which

22.text: by their lineage or tastes fraternize with the reindeer-breeders; while the

23.text: ceremonial of Kereˊtkun predominates among the Maritime people in the

24.text: proper sense of the word. There are, however, reindeer-breeding families who

29.text: the vent-hole being carefully closed for the purpose. Heads of the walrus,

30.text: seal, and other animals, serve as necessary objects for the ceremony. It is

31.text: not obligatory to preserve the heads of all animals killed in the hunt, and

32.text: even a few suffice. The sacrifice is performed outside of the tent by the

33.text: younger members of the family, who throw blood-soup, meat, and all kinds
